newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower, acreage shift talk hits Dec.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower, acreage shift talk hits Dec.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a technical setback with new crop December coming under added pressure on talk of a possible increase in corn acreage this year in the U.S., traders said.
Traders said there was talk about a story implying a shift in Conservation Reserve Program acres into corn acreage.
"There was a CRP story talking about more acres," a trader said.
U.S. lawmakers and farm groups said Wednesday the USDA may be overloading itself by promising to enroll up to 22 million acres of land in the CRP by early summer.
But traders said corn set back because it was overbought and soybeans again led the way. Soybeans Tuesday surged on aggressive fund buying. Fund demand was slow Wednesday.
"Without the funds to support us today we were due for a correction and we got it," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
There was no significant shift in fundamentals to drive the market with a slight hike in producer selling late Tuesday and early Wednesday lending mild pressure.
Corn closed 1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 1/2 at $2.92-3/4.

The market Tuesday absorbed bearish input from the USDA Agricultural Outlook Conference and took in stride an estimate for a 9.6-billion-bushel corn crop this year from closely-watched private analytical firm Sparks Companies.
A Sparks Companies official Tuesday spoke to the Outlook Conference.

Export news early Wednesday included a USDA announcement of a sale of 164,592 tonnes of U.S. corn to an unknown destination. Also Taiwan overnight bought 24,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and there was news a South Korean firm was seeking 50,000 tonnes of Chinese corn.
Commercial buying Tuesday was supportive but the market remains poised to shift depending on action by key funds.
Wednesday, ADM Investor Services sold two million bushels of March, Cargill Inc sold two million May and Prudential Securities sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Refco Inc bought two million bushels of May and Tenco Inc bought three million bushels of May, traders said.
Technicians early Wednesday reported a bullish slant to the four and 20-day moving averages.
First support in March corn was at $2.89 and second support was at $2.83. The session low was $2.91-1/4.
First resistance was at $2.95-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.01-1/2. The session high was $2.94-3/4.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 78 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 95,000 contracts, below the 104,070 traded Tuesday.
In corn options, Refco Inc bought 800 May $2.70 calls at 25 to 25-1/2 cents, LFG Futures bought 500 December $2.90 calls and sold 500 December $2.70 puts at 15 to 18-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, below the 22,636 traded Tuesday.
